title: CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Evaluation
file_title: CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Evaluation – Appendix 3: Stage 2 Econometric Report
description: This document describes an evaluation of the UK's Carbon Reduction Commitment (CRC) Energy Efficiency Scheme, which targets large non-intensive energy users to promote energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions. The evaluation, conducted by a partnership including CAG Consultants and Databuild, utilized a mixed-method approach comprising surveys, interviews, and econometric analysis. Findings suggest that the CRC has positively influenced energy efficiency, particularly in the private sector, leading to a 3-5% annual reduction in electricity consumption and significant gas savings for high-use organizations from 2010 to 2012. The scheme has also heightened energy efficiency awareness at the board level, driven by financial and reputational factors, although barriers such as funding and policy coherence remain. Despite initial administrative challenges, the CRC has improved in customer satisfaction and has been deemed cost-effective, with investments paying back within five years and additional benefits like enhanced CSR image and employee engagement. The evaluation concludes that the CRC has significantly impacted energy efficiency behavior and emissions, but recommends clearer strategic oversight and consistent government policy.

title: Evaluation of the Big Energy Saving Network: Final Report
file_title: Evaluation of the Big Energy Saving Network: final report
description: This document describes an evaluation of the Big Energy Saving Network (BESN) program, designed to help vulnerable individuals reduce energy costs by offering advice on energy markets and support mechanisms. The evaluation, conducted through surveys, interviews, and data analysis, found that the program reached around 94,000 consumers, with many reporting increased empowerment and taking actions such as switching energy tariffs. Despite its success in engaging diverse groups and being praised for its design and training, the program faced challenges in reaching certain demographics and providing comprehensive training on the Energy Company Obligation (ECO). The evaluation suggests that future iterations should include more in-depth training, flexible support, and targeted outreach. The BESN program was effective in increasing consumer empowerment, with a majority feeling more informed and taking energy-saving steps, although few signed up for an ECO assessment. The program's success was attributed to the experience of the workers, interactive workshops, and personalized support. While there were difficulties in reaching some vulnerable groups and a low rate of provider switching, the program exceeded engagement targets and contributed to market reform. Recommendations for the future include enhancing training and sustaining changes in consumer attitudes and behaviors. Overall, the BESN program met most of its expected outcomes and was delivered as intended.

title: Green Deal Communities Private Rental Sector Incentive Report of Findings
file_title: Annex 1 - qualitative research report
description: This document describes an evaluation of the Green Deal Communities Private Rental Sector incentive, a policy designed to enhance energy efficiency in rental properties to mitigate carbon emissions. Conducted by Ipsos MORI, the evaluation employed qualitative research methods, including stakeholder interviews, to examine the policy's implementation, marketing, and participant motivations. Landlords were motivated by financial returns, tenant satisfaction, and maintenance considerations, while tenant engagement was low. Marketing success varied, with targeted and personalized communication showing some effectiveness, though measurement was hindered by inadequate data recording. Obstacles such as costs, planning regulations, and procedural delays were identified. Recommendations include early engagement with letting agents and establishing a single contact point to streamline the process. The evaluation also assessed the broader Green Deal scheme's impact in the PRS, noting the importance of local authority trust and the challenges posed by the Green Deal Finance scheme's complexity. The findings aim to guide the Department of Energy and Climate Change in refining energy efficiency initiatives.

title: Independent Evaluation of FID Enabling for Renewables Final Report to the Department of Energy and Climate Change
file_title: EMR and FID Enabling for Renewables government response
description: This document summarizes independent evaluations of the FID Enabling for Renewables project, aimed at reducing investment uncertainty in the renewable energy sector during regulatory transitions. The evaluations, conducted by Grant Thornton UK LLP, employed literature reviews, interviews, quantitative and qualitative analyses, and stakeholder research. Findings revealed that the project effectively awarded Investment Contracts to several projects, aiding in meeting EU renewable targets, but faced issues with under-resourcing, transparency, and a limited technology mix, which could affect future competition and prices. Recommendations included better documentation, improved transparency, and enhanced monitoring. The evaluations also emphasized the need for clear policy frameworks, robust business case structures, and certainty to attract investment, while suggesting improvements in communication, decision-making processes, and structured business cases for future initiatives. Despite some challenges in transparency, communication, and consistency, the process was considered robust, with recommendations for clearer guidelines and methodology to ensure fair competition in future projects.

title: Independent evaluation of the Electricity Market Reform Final Report to the Department of Energy and Climate Change
file_title: EMR and FID Enabling for Renewables government response
description: This document describes a comprehensive evaluation of the UK's Electricity Market Reform (EMR), focusing on the Capacity Market (CM) and Contracts for Difference (CfD) schemes. The EMR's primary goals are to secure electricity supply, encourage investment in low-carbon technologies, and minimize costs. The evaluation, conducted by various entities, employed detailed policy analysis, stakeholder research, and auction process reviews. Results show that while the CM and CfD have attracted investment and capacity, there are concerns about their long-term effectiveness, potential conflicts within the EMR, and alignment with decarbonization goals. Recommendations include stabilizing the CM framework, enhancing transparency, and ensuring regular policy interaction reviews. Specific issues such as the reliance on reciprocating engines and the impact of power station closures were noted. The evaluation concludes that despite the presence of effective policy instruments, their complexity warrants continuous monitoring and adjustment to meet the overarching objectives of the EMR.

title: Mid-term evaluation of the performance of the operations of Micro in Haiti
file_title: DFID Management response to the Mid-term evaluation of the performance of the operations of MiCRO in Haiti
description: This document describes a summary of evaluations for the Microinsurance Catastrophe Risk Organization (MiCRO), a program aimed at offering index-based insurance to Haitian microentrepreneurs, especially women, to safeguard against natural disasters and bolster economic resilience. The evaluations, conducted by different entities including the Caribbean Development Bank and International Financial Consulting Ltd., utilized various methods such as stakeholder interviews, focus groups, risk modeling, and document analysis. Despite initial successes, such as enrolling 50,000 borrowers, the evaluations consistently found that MiCRO struggled with challenges like insufficient funding, administrative inefficiencies, inadequate marketing, and inaccurate risk models, which hindered its developmental goals and led to the cancellation of certain insurance components. The program also faced sustainability issues, technical expertise gaps, and stakeholder misalignment. Recommendations for improvement were made, emphasizing the need for better risk data, technical leadership, sufficient capital, and a comprehensive business strategy. The evaluations aim to provide learning opportunities for future microinsurance initiatives rather than assigning blame.

title: Research into the Green Deal and Eco Programme supply chain (follow-up study)
file_title: Research into the Green Deal and ECO Programme Supply Chain (Follow-up Study)
description: This document describes an evaluation of the Green Deal (GD) and Energy Companies Obligation (ECO) supply chain, as well as the Green Deal Home Improvement Fund (GDHIF), focusing on their impact on suppliers, installers, and the distribution of work. The evaluation, which included interviews with over 700 industry professionals and data analysis, found that the market is dominated by a small number of suppliers, with many being micro businesses certified for a single role. Results showed a skewed distribution of assessments and installations, with a significant portion of professionals' sales and income coming from GD/ECO programs. There was mixed optimism about future demand, with some installers facing delays due to finance-related issues. The GDHIF was found to have engaged installers to varying degrees, with some not fully prepared for the scheme's launch or close. Challenges identified include lead generation, customer targeting, the complexity of certification, and the impact of accreditation costs on participation. Overall, while the GD and ECO programs have increased demand for energy efficiency services, there are notable challenges in the supply chain and installer experiences.
